1.note: חרי"ב, "the sage R. Y. B.": probably R. Jacob Burla, emissary of Jerusalem. In A. Freimann, Ma'agal Tov ha-Shalem (Berlin–Jerusalem 1921–34) he is named in full (חר"י בורלא) in Livorno with R. Yom Tov Algazi (p. 69), and as חרי"ב in Venice, where the council gave him travel money (p. 85); this identification was proposed by GPT and fits both passages.

2.note: So printed (checked on the scan); the word לאבו is not clear. The sense seems to be that he also set his face to make light of the Ḥida.

3.note: An abbreviation for a body of the Venetian community, probably a council (va'ad); not resolved further.

4.note: Read as "the festival" (חג ה...), that is Sukkot, since the next item is the first of its intermediate days.

5.note: Read as Friuli (Italian il Friuli); the route to Modena by way of Gradisca is not explained.

6.note: 5537 was a leap year. 11 Adar II was Thursday 20 March 1777, and the next dates (the weeks of Shemini and Tazria) follow it; 11 Adar I was Tuesday 18 February 1777.

7.note: Printed סדר הכס"א; A. Freimann, Ma'agal Tov ha-Shalem (Berlin–Jerusalem 1921–34), p. 91, reads סדר הנש"א and identifies R. Nathan Shapira, the Jerusalem kabbalist (Ashkenazi). In this type נ/כ and ש/ס are easily confused.

8.note: Read as the family name Valle; the initials do not fit Moses David Valle of Padua, so the person is not identified.

9.note: Printed ליפשין מאיכנשין; A. Freimann, Ma'agal Tov ha-Shalem (Berlin–Jerusalem 1921–34), p. 91, reads משה ליפשיץ מחינטשין: R. Moses Lipschitz of Chęciny (Poland), who taught in Modena.

11.note: Italian inoculazione: inoculation against smallpox, then debated by Italian rabbis.

12.note: Abbreviation of a family name: de Roquemartine, a Jewish family of Carpentras; A. Freimann, Ma'agal Tov ha-Shalem (Berlin–Jerusalem 1921–34) names him so in a note ("de Roquemartine").
